title: No. 11 Notre Dame Beats No. 1 Miami 31-24 in South Bend
dek: Luke Talich's third-quarter interception and end-zone pass breakup sealed a 31-24 Notre Dame win over the top-ranked Hurricanes, their first loss of the season.
author: Meridian Newsroom

image.alt: View of the football stadium at the University of Notre Dame from premium seating

keyPoints: No. 11 Notre Dame beat No. 1 Miami 31-24 on Saturday night in South Bend, handing the Hurricanes their first loss of the season.
Notre Dame led 24-3 early in the third quarter before Miami cut the margin to seven.
Talich intercepted Darian Mensah near midfield in the third quarter, then knocked away a late end-zone pass to Elija Lofton.
CJ Carr finished 29-of-40 for 319 yards and three touchdowns for the Irish; Mensah was 24-of-43 for 276 yards.
body:
No. 11 Notre Dame beat No. 1 Miami 31-24 on Saturday night in South Bend. It was Miami's first loss of the season, and Notre Dame closed as 7.5-point favorites.

## The turning point

Notre Dame led 24-3 early in the third quarter. Miami cut the lead to seven and had the ball near midfield with a chance to tie the game. Luke Talich jumped in front of a pass intended for Elija Lofton and intercepted it, Mensah's second interception of the season, per Yahoo Sports. Notre Dame then went back up by two scores: CJ Carr found a wide-open Nolan James Jr. on fourth down for a 36-yard catch-and-run, and James scored on a run.

## The finish

With 3:36 left, Mensah appeared to find Lofton in the end zone for what could have been a game-tying touchdown. ESPN's recap reports that Lofton's feet appeared to land in bounds, but Talich knocked the ball out of his hands, and officials ruled that he did not complete the catch. Notre Dame took over on downs, and Miami's final drive ended with a sack on its first play.

## The numbers

Carr was 29-of-40 for 319 yards and three touchdowns. Miami ran 28 times for 101 yards. Mensah threw his second interception of the season. Cooper Barkate had 10 catches for 92 yards and two touchdowns, and Lofton had seven catches for 113 yards and a touchdown.

## Playoff picture

Notre Dame entered the weekend at No. 11 in the first College Football Playoff rankings, which the committee released Nov. 3, and had been criticized for lacking a signature win. The Irish have three remaining games against unranked opponents: Boston College, SMU and Syracuse. Miami remains the favorite to win the ACC, according to Yahoo Sports.

## Earlier preview

The game was previewed as the marquee matchup of a Saturday with six ranked-versus-ranked games. The Athletic called it the week's game of the week.
